issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a tensor-network helper named create_zero_state(num_qubits), but the template repository defines the corresponding stub under the different name init_zero_state(num_qubits). This mismatch means students looking for the required function (create_zero_state) will not find the intended implementation site in the template, causing unnecessary confusion about where to implement the zero-state MPS and increasing extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template stub name match the problem statement and solution. Rename the template function init_zero_state to create_zero_state(num_qubits) (or add a small wrapper:def create_zero_state(num_qubits): return init_zero_state(num_qubits)). This aligns the template with the stated API and the solution, removing the mapping hurdle for students.
